prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"Hi, I need a rosé gift for my boss that tastes a bit like flowers, isn't too heavy, and costs under 25 euros."

List A:
Wine 1: Gewürztraminer, France, $90. Tasting note: "The heady scent of Damask rose hints unmistakably to Gewürztraminer. The palate follows lusciously, generously and luxuriantly: wonderfully sweet notions of peach, ripe apricot and yellow mirabelle plum are perfumed with a rose petal scent but are also pervaded by a gentle citrus freshness that lifts everything. The length is astonishing and dreamy. This is dangerously delicious."
Wine 2: Rosé, US, $10. Tasting note: "A good deal for a dry rosé that's almost red like a light Pinot Noir. Very low in alcohol at 12.5%, it's light throughout with layers of peach and grenadine."
Wine 3: Pinot Noir, US, $24. Tasting note: "Break out the prosciutto-wrapped figs and stuffed mushroom appetizers for this light, silky rosé. It's crisp in acidity and delicate in the mouth, with assertive raspberry, orange tea and honey flavors. This is one of the more successful Pinot Noir rosés out there."
Wine 4: Rosé, US, $16. Tasting note: "Very dry and a little austere, with suggestions of cherry skins, citrus fruits and spices. The alcohol is nice and low, while the acidity is brisk. A fine, elegant rosé, delicate and easy to drink."
Wine 5: Nebbiolo, Italy, price unknown. Tasting note: "One of the best Barolos of the year, Coste di Rose is a natural beauty with gorgeous, thick extraction and perfectly balanced aromas of blueberries, violets, almond paste, sweet spice and root beer. The wine shows impressive heft and density, yet it is elegant and polished at the same time with finely textured tannins. Cellar this delightful wine ten years or more."

List B:
Wine 1: Rosé, US, $12. Tasting note: "Just what you want in a rosé, at a good price. It's a robust wine, dryish and spicy, with a creamy mouthfeel framing pleasant raspberry, cherry, prosciutto and vanilla flavors."
Wine 2: Champagne Blend, France, $87. Tasting note: "A rosé Champagne with aromas and flavors of cherries and strawberries blended with dry spices, like cinnamon. This would make a festive apéritif this holiday season."
Wine 3: Cabernet Franc, US, $30. Tasting note: "A scintillating scent of rose petals opens up this pleasing wine, which continues with raspberry and cherry fruit, accented with light milk chocolate. It is not a heavy wine; in fact, if Franc can ever be called elegant, even feminine, this is how it should taste. The finish falls off rather quickly, but otherwise it is a fine effort."
Wine 4: Rosé, US, $12. Tasting note: "This is a great option for a widely available and affordable rosé. A very pretty pink in color, it shows baked strawberry, rose petals and vanilla ice cream on the nose. The sip tightens around cherry and strawberry-brioche flavors."
Wine 5: Rosé, France, $30. Tasting note: "A fragrant, fresh rosé that is full of red fruits and tight acidity. Crisp and bright, it makes a delicious summer refresher. Drink now."

Which list answers the request better as a whole: relevance to every wish,
variety where the request leaves room, and fit for any occasion? If they
are equally good, say tie. Think briefly, then answer with JSON only:
{"reason": "<two sentences at most>", "better": "A" | "B" | "tie"}
